supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Veneta classic with soaring Dark Star and tight China>Rider
ai_show_review.blurb: The setlist is packed with a blistering Dark Star → El Paso, a flawless China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider transition, and a thunderous Playing In The Band that drives the second set. Jerry’s guitar shines throughout while Keith adds cavernous textures, and Phil delivers a powerhouse bass solo in Dark Star.
ai_show_review.review: The August 27, 1972 show at the Old Renaissance Faire Grounds in Veneta is often cited as one of the peak moments of the spring‑'72 tour. From the opening burst of The Promised Land into Sugaree and Deal, the band quickly finds a groove that erupts on China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider – a segue reviewers describe as “locked‑in” and “cavernous.” The second set explodes with Playing In The Band, building into an ecstatic crescendo that propels He’s Gone, Jack Straw and Bird Song. The centerpiece is the 30‑plus minute Dark Star that seamlessly segues into El Paso, showcasing Jerry’s soaring lead lines and Phil’s “phunky” bass solo. The night closes on a high note with Sugar Magnolia and One More Saturday Night, leaving fans with a feeling of pure, unfiltered joy. All seven soundboard recordings capture the performance in crystal‑clear detail, but the Hollister SBD (gd1972-08-27.sbd.hollister.2199.sbeok.shnf) stands out for its pristine mix and lack of any audible flaws.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard source with crystal‑clear mix, perfect balance and no dropouts – captures every nuance of the legendary performance.

key_highlights: Smoking Dark Star → El Paso with soaring guitar leads.
Seamless China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider transition that locks the band in.
Explosive Playing In The Band crescendo powering the second set.
Exceptional soundboard recordings capture every nuance of this legendary Veneta night.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is described as perfect and fire‑brand – his solos on Dark Star, Playing In The Band and the El Paso transition are blistering and full of adventurous phrasing.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh delivers a powerful, “phunky” bass foundation; his solo in Dark Star is highlighted as a standout moment, and he stays tight throughout the high‑energy jams.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s rhythm guitar locks tightly with the band on Bertha and the rockers, while his vocal delivery adds emotional weight to ballads like Sugaree.
band_performance.Keith: Keyboard work is cavernous and essential, providing spacey textures that lift the Playin’ crescendo and add depth to Dark Star and Bird Song.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart’s drumming drives the extended improvisations with relentless energy, especially evident in the Dark Star/El Paso stretch.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann supplies a fierce, driving pulse that underpins the entire set, propelling the high‑intensity moments of Playing In The Band and the final encores.
